title: Say It Again, Walter
subject: a woman in her sixties fitted with her first hearing aids, who sits in the car outside the audiologist's office and hears her husband Walter humming along to the radio, something he has apparently done for years
caption: Philly soul, early 70s sweet soul style. Lush sweeping string section, shimmering vibraphone, Fender Rhodes chords, a warm French horn line, tight bass and four-on-the-floor drum pocket with hi-hat sixteenths. Silky mix with wide strings and soft plate reverb. Female alto lead, warm and glowing, gliding into a sweet head voice, smooth three-part backing harmonies. 96 BPM, E major. Warm, grateful and glowing. No trap drums, no autotune, no rock guitar, no modern EDM, no rap.
lyrics:
[Intro - strings and vibraphone]

[Verse 1]
Two small beige things behind my ears
The lady said give it a week
I climbed into the car with Walter
And something hummed beside me

[Pre-Chorus]
Low and a little flat
Right along with the radio

[Chorus]
Say it again, Walter
Hum it one more time
Thirty years beside me
And I missed the line

[Verse 2]
He went red right to his collar
Said, I always hum, my dear
I said turn the radio up
I've got some catching up to do

[Pre-Chorus]
Low and a little flat
Sweetest thing on Route 9

[Chorus]
Say it again, Walter
Don't you dare stop now
Thirty years of humming
And I'm hearing it right now

[Bridge - horns and strings]
The turn signal ticking
The kettle when we're home

[Outro - backing vocals]
Say it again, Walter
Hum me all the way home
